Subject: Deep Depression over coastal Myanmar weakened into a Depression over 
Myanmar and adjoining Eastcentral & Northeast Bay of Bengal 
The Deep Depression over coastal Myanmar moved north-northwestwards with a speed of 28 
kmph during past 6 hours, weakened into a Depression and lay centred at 0530 hrs IST of today, 
the 29th September 2026 over  Myanmar and adjoining Eastcentral & Northeast Bay of Bengal 
near latitude 18.9°N and longitude 96.0°E, about 50 km west of Toungoo (Myanmar), 80 km east 
of Pyay (Myanmar), 180 km north-northwest of Bago (Myanmar) ,  210 km north-northwest of 
Kyaikto (Myanmar) and 240 km northeast of Yangon (Myanmar).  
It is very likely to move further north-northwestwards and weaken into a well marked low pressure 
area over Myanmar and a djoining southeast Bangladesh & Northeast Bay of Bengal  around 
evening of today, the 29th September. Thereafter, it is very likely to continue to move further north-
northwestwards towards southeast Bangladesh & adjoining areas of Myanmar, Mizoram, Tripura 
& Northeast Bay of Bengal and weaken gradually during subsequent 24 hours.  
Forecast track and intensity are given in the following table:

Warnings: 
(i) Rainfall Warning: 
❖ Light to moderate rainfall at most places with isolated heavy rainfall very likely over Andaman 
& Nicobar Islands on 29th September. 
❖ Light to moderate rainfall at many places with isolated heavy rainfall very likely over Mizoram 
& Tripura on 29th & 30th September. 
 
(ii) Wind warning: 
India Meteorological Department 
 (Ministry of Earth Sciences) 
 

❖ Squally weather with wind speed reaching 45-55 kmph gusting to 65 kmph is prevailing over 
North Andaman Sea, along & off Myanmar coast and likely to decrease becoming 40-50 kmph 
gusting to 60 kmph by today noon and decrease gradually thereafter. 
❖ Squally weather with wind speed reaching 45-55 kmph gusting to 65 kmph is prevailing over 
adjoining areas of Eastcentral Bay of Bengal and is likely to decrease becoming 40-50 gusting 
to 60 kmph from noon of 29th September and decrease gradually thereafter. 
❖ Squally weather with wind speed reaching 30-40 kmph gusting to 50 kmph over northeast Bay 
of Bengal and along & off Bangladesh coast till morning of 30th September, 2026 and decrease 
gradually thereafter. 
(iii) Sea condition: 
 
❖ Very Rough to rough Sea condition is very likely over North Andaman Sea & adjoining areas of 
Eastcentral Bay of Bengal  and along & off Myanmar coast till 29th September evening . 
Thereafter, it is very likely to improve becoming rough to moderate from 29th September night 
onwards and improve further gradually. 
❖ Rough to moderate sea condition is very likely over adjoining areas of northeast Bay of Bengal 
and along & off Myanmar - Bangladesh coasts till 30th morning and improve thereafter. 
(iv) Fishermen warnings: 
Fishermen are advised not to venture into North Andaman Sea & adjoining areas of eastcentral 
Bay of Bengal and along & off Myanmar coast on 29th September and into northeast Bay of Bengal 
and along & off Bangladesh-Myanmar coasts till morning of 30th September, 2026.  
(v) Impact expected & Action Suggested (Andaman Islands, Miz oram and Tripura for 
squally wind & heavy rainfall): 
Impact expected: 
❖ Breaking of tree branches, uprooting of small trees like banana, papaya, drum sticks. 
❖ Strong wind and rain may damage plantation, horticulture and standing crops. 
❖ Partial damage to vulnerable structures due to strong winds and rain. 
❖ There could be localised landslides, mudslides, landslips in hilly areas and water logging, 
inundation and flooding over low-lying areas. 
❖ Onshore and offshore operations may get affected. 
❖ Small ships, trawlers and boats may be affected. 
❖ Occasional reduction in visibility due to heavy rainfall. 
❖ Helicopter services may get affected. 
Action suggested: 
❖ People are advised to keep a watch on the weather for worsening conditions and be ready to 
move to safer places accordingly.  
❖ Surface transport may be regulated. 
❖ Fishing operation may be suspended.  
❖ Tourism and recreational activities to be regulated. 
❖ Onshore and offshore activities to be judiciously regulated. 
❖ Helicopter services to be regulated. 
 
Next bulletin will be issued at 1130 hours IST of today, the 29th September, 2026. 
 
(Monica Sharma ) 
IMD, New Delhi
